ideas.hypothesis: Urbanization raises later per-capita output only when non-agricultural employment grows alongside it. 'Urbanization without industrialization' (urban population share rising faster than non-farm jobs) has no causal growth effect, which would explain the mixed findings on two-way causality.

sources.role: method: econometric analysis of feedback between urbanization and economic development
finding: review of consensus and controversy on urbanization-development mechanisms, developing vs developed countries, China
mechanism: evolutionary rather than mechanistic view of development

ideas.test: Chinese provincial or prefecture panel, 1990-2018: panel VAR/Granger causality plus threshold regression of GDP-per-capita growth on lagged urbanization. The threshold variable is the gap between urban population share and non-agricultural employment share.
ideas.disconfirming: Urbanization predicts growth equally whatever the urbanization-employment gap, or no threshold is detected.

ideas.hypothesis: SROI ratios reported for social and development programs systematically exceed benefit-cost ratios computed from RCT effect estimates for the same or comparable programs, because SROI relies on stakeholder-reported outcomes and assumed deadweight and attribution rather than on experimental counterfactuals.

sources.role: method: SROI stages applied to a children's camp program, monetizing social, environmental and economic outcomes
method: distinguishes RCTs from outcome studies and describes types of economic evaluation
setting: evolution of methods for assessing economic development impacts

ideas.test: Meta-comparison of about 30 programs (cash transfers, health, job training) that have both a published SROI report and an RCT evaluation. Compute RCT-based benefit-cost ratios with standard valuations, test whether SROI/BCR exceeds 1, and check whether deadweight and attribution assumptions explain the gap.
ideas.disconfirming: SROI ratios are not systematically higher than RCT-based ratios, or the two methods rank programs the same way.

ideas.hypothesis: Better infrastructure raises national competitiveness more where institutions are strong, so the marginal effect of infrastructure on competitiveness (outside the infrastructure pillar itself) depends on governance.

sources.role: finding and measure: infrastructure as a determinant of growth and Global Competitiveness Index standing
mechanism: supply-chain, labor-market and trade impacts of transport projects
setting: how economic policy contributed to Australia's development

ideas.test: Panel of about 130 countries, 2007-2017, from WEF Global Competitiveness Reports. Regress changes in the GCI score excluding the infrastructure pillar, and GDP growth, on the lagged infrastructure pillar interacted with the institutions pillar, with country fixed effects and lagged public investment as an instrument.
ideas.disconfirming: The infrastructure x institutions interaction is null, or infrastructure has no effect on non-infrastructure competitiveness once country trends are controlled.

ideas.hypothesis: Ex-ante assessments of transportation projects that include supply-chain, labor-market access and trade impacts predict ex-post local employment and output changes more accurately than assessments based only on user cost savings.

sources.role: method: evolution of impact assessment from business cost savings to supply-chain, labor and trade impacts
method: stochastic optimization for highway project trade-off analysis
mechanism: market-economy theory applied to transport development

ideas.test: Collect about 50 completed highway or intermodal projects with archived ex-ante appraisals of both types. Estimate realized county employment and output effects with project-level synthetic controls, then compare forecast errors across the two appraisal approaches.
ideas.disconfirming: Broader-impact methods forecast realized outcomes no better than cost-saving methods, or overpredict benefits by more.

ideas.hypothesis: In urban areas, more deprived neighborhoods have higher overall spatial accessibility to food retailers but a higher ratio of fast-food/convenience access to supermarket access. That composition, not total access, predicts household food consumption patterns.

sources.role: method and finding: Enhanced Two-Step Floating Catchment Area model; generally higher access to all food retailers in deprived urban NZ areas
setting: planning new communities for health and wellbeing

ideas.test: Apply E2SFCA to geocoded food retailers in two or three cities, by area deprivation index. Link to household survey diet or food-expenditure data and regress dietary outcomes on the healthy-to-unhealthy accessibility ratio, controlling for household income.
ideas.disconfirming: Deprived areas do not have a higher unhealthy-to-healthy access ratio, or diet outcomes are unrelated to the ratio once income is controlled.

ideas.hypothesis: Interior Chinese counties (Northwest and Southwest) that received relocated factories, schools and infrastructure during the Second Sino-Japanese War show persistently higher industrialization and income decades later than comparable interior counties that received none.

sources.role: setting and finding: motivation, achievements and failures of Northwest wartime economic development
setting: stages of Republican-era development in Guangxi
mechanism: evolutionary path dependence in development

ideas.test: County-level dataset mapping wartime relocated enterprises (historical records 1937-1945). Compare industrial employment shares in the 1982 and 2000 censuses and later GDP per capita with neighboring non-recipient counties, controlling for pre-war characteristics and using distance to wartime transport routes as an instrument.
ideas.disconfirming: Recipient counties show no persistent advantage once pre-war characteristics are controlled, or any advantage is gone by 1982.

ideas.hypothesis: Lower TELRIC-based prices for unbundled network elements raised entrants' market share but cut incumbent carriers' network investment, so states with lower UNE rates saw slower later infrastructure upgrades by incumbents.

sources.role: mechanism: TELRIC pricing, entry, incumbent asset values and the vintage and type of capital under competition

ideas.test: US state panel 1997-2006: state-commission UNE loop rates, incumbent capex and broadband deployment (ARMIS, FCC Form 477). Regress incumbent investment on UNE rates with state and year fixed effects, instrumenting rates with commission composition.
ideas.disconfirming: UNE rates are unrelated to incumbent investment, or lower rates go with higher incumbent investment (competitive pressure dominating).

ideas.hypothesis: Regional classifications from hierarchical clustering of economic, social and ecological indicators are more stable over time, and better predict later regional growth, than rankings based on a single integral efficiency index.

sources.role: method: integral assessment of regional development efficiency across Ukraine's regions (economic, social, ecological)
method: hierarchical clustering to identify economic models across EU-28
method: factor-analysis indicator system for evaluating the development environment

ideas.test: Ukrainian oblast data 2005-2019: build both an integral-index ranking and hierarchical clusters from the same indicators for 2005-2012. Compare year-to-year membership stability (adjusted Rand index) and out-of-sample prediction of 2013-2019 gross regional product growth.
ideas.disconfirming: Cluster membership is no more stable and no more predictive than integral-index ranks.

ideas.hypothesis: Conventional four-step travel demand models over-predict vehicle trips and VMT for smart-growth developments (mixed use, near transit, walkable), and post-processors for density, diversity, design and destinations reduce this bias.

sources.role: method: Caltrans-sponsored modeling of the travel impacts of smart-growth strategies
finding: review of urban form and travel evidence and its methodological limits
method: micro-scale outcome measurement in transport system design

ideas.test: Select 20-30 completed infill/TOD developments with archived pre-opening traffic forecasts and collect post-occupancy trip counts. Compare forecast errors of unadjusted model outputs with those of the same forecasts after 4D adjustment.
ideas.disconfirming: Unadjusted models do not over-predict trips at smart-growth sites, or 4D adjustment does not reduce forecast error.

ideas.hypothesis: Regions that combine local talent development with talent introduction (recruitment) achieve higher firm innovation rates than regions that pursue either alone, because local training raises the capacity to absorb imported skills.

sources.role: mechanism: need to coordinate talent development and talent introduction in the West Straits Economic Zone
measure: an innovation census of firms in an Australian state

ideas.test: Panel of Chinese prefectures (or Australian states), 2008-2018, coding talent development (higher-education and vocational spending) and talent-introduction programs. Regress firm innovation rates (innovation survey or patents per firm) on each policy and their interaction, with region and year fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: The interaction is null or negative, or innovation responds only to introduction policies.
